title: Structs, dictionaries, and stable reports
summary: Aggregate sensor readings with value types, then fix a report whose dictionary order changes between runs.

objectives.description: Accumulate reading totals in a dictionary.
Find the source of unstable dictionary output.
Apply value semantics to a copied record.

hints: A struct copies its stored properties when assigned.
reduce(into:) threads the dictionary through each reading.
Subscript with a default so the first reading starts at zero.
Sort the dictionary entries by key before printing.

misconceptions.description: Adding to a dictionary key that has no value yet.
misconceptions.testDescription: The totals accumulate per sensor with a default of zero.
misconceptions.feedback: A missing dictionary key returns nil. Subscript with default: 0 before adding so the first reading creates the entry.

misconceptions.description: Expecting a struct copy to share storage.
misconceptions.feedback: Assigning or passing a struct copies its value. Changing the copy does not change the original.

misconceptions.description: Replacing the dictionary instead of stabilizing its presentation.
misconceptions.feedback: Changing the data model does not fix the report order and may lose the lookup. Sort the entries when printing.

misconceptions.description: Counting readings instead of adding their values.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Incrementing the sensor total by one per reading instead of adding reading.value.
misconceptions.feedback: The report needs a sum. Add reading.value, not one, so multiple readings accumulate correctly.

sections.title: Structs are value types
sections.body: A struct such as struct Reading { let sensor: String; let value: Int } stores its properties inline. Assignment and parameter passing copy the value, so a report cannot change the caller's array by accident. The compiler also provides a memberwise initializer. Use let for fields that never change and var only for state that must mutate.

sections.title: Group and accumulate
sections.body: Dictionary(grouping:by:) groups values under a key, while reduce(into:) accumulates without creating intermediate copies. totals[reading.sensor, default: 0] += reading.value reads a missing key as zero and stores the new total. mapValues transforms a dictionary's values and keeps its keys.

sections.title: Sort before presenting
sections.body: A Dictionary is unordered, so iterating it can produce a different order each run. Sorting entries with report.sorted { $0.key < $1.key } gives a deterministic report. If order carries meaning in the domain, keep an array of records and derive the dictionary only for lookup.

vocabulary.definition: Copying a value produces an independent value with its own storage.
The struct initializer the compiler generates from its stored properties.
An accumulation that mutates a single result value in place.
A value used when a dictionary key is absent, written dictionary[key, default:].

Passing it copies the stored properties.

quiz.prompt: A Reading value is passed to a function that builds a corrected record with a new initializer. What does the caller's original value show?

options.label: The corrected values, because both names share one object.
A compile error, because structs are immutable.
nil, because the value was moved into the function.

quiz.explanation: A Swift struct has value semantics. The function receives a copy, and returning a different record does not modify the caller's value.
